 Blog Marrakech Film Festival 2026: Dates, Jury and Access
 Marrakech Film Festival 2026: 23rd edition, 20 to 28 November, jury chaired by Marion Cotillard, free e-pass from 26 October, venues and access.
 October 21, 2026 
 18 min 
 Read article 
 Magazine 
 Table of Contents
 Loading...

The Marrakech Film Festival 2026 runs from 20 to 28 November 2026. Its jury is chaired by Marion Cotillard, the French actress and Oscar winner, announced on 13 October 2026. The public e-pass is free, for ages 18 and over, and opens on 26 October 2026. The detailed programme had not been published as of 21 October 2026.
 Checked on 21 October 2026 against the official sources cited (the festival’s accreditation page, the 2026 rules) and the Moroccan press. 
 The 23rd edition of the Marrakech International Film Festival runs from 20 to 28 November 2026. The public gets into the films and the conversations with a free e-pass, open to people aged 18 and over. This guide sets out what is confirmed as of 21 October 2026, separates the 2026 edition from the 2025 one, and flags what is still to be checked: the detailed programme, the official selection and the cinema ticket prices. Each venue reported only by the press is marked as such.
 1. Dates, jury and public access in 2026
Photo by JR Harris 
on Unsplash Marrakech International Film Festival 2026
 20 to 28 November 2026 
 Free public e-pass 
 Hivernage, venues to be confirmed 
 November: around 21 °C by day Organised by the Foundation of the Marrakech International Film Festival, the event is in its 23rd edition. The dates appear on the official accreditation page , and the 2026 rules and the Moroccan press confirm them.
 Highlights 
 An international competition of 14 films, first and second features. 
 A top prize, the Étoile d’Or, worth USD 50,000 according to the 2026 rules. 
 A professional strand, the Ateliers de l’Atlas, from 22 to 26 November. 
 For the public, the rule is simple: films and conversations with personalities are free to attend with an e-pass, provided you are 18 or over. The detailed schedule had not yet been published when this guide was written.
 Pixidia tip: get ready to register from 26 October 2026. The e-pass and the access code arrive by email and are used in the Marrakech Festival App. Between screenings, a private guided tour of the souks helps you find your way around the medina. From the medina, the Palais des Congrès is about 15 minutes away by taxi, according to Marrakech Cityguide.
 Marrakech Shopping Tours: Private Souks Tour 
€39.38 per adult (based on 2 adults), checked on 21 October 2026 for the festival dates
· ★ 4.96 ( 451 reviews) 
Book my souks tour 
 Key dates of the 23rd edition, as of 21 October 2026 Step Date Status 
 Film submissions close 31 July 2026 Past 
 Jury announced, chaired by Marion Cotillard 13 October 2026 Past 
 E-pass registration opens (public and professionals) 26 October 2026 Announced 
 Press registration closes 31 October 2026 Announced 
 Official selection announced Early November 2026 Expected 
 Ateliers de l’Atlas 22 to 26 November 2026 Announced 
 Festival, from opening to closing 20 to 28 November 2026 Confirmed 
 Source: festival accreditations , 2026 rules and Le360 (in French, 19 October 2026) , checked on 21 October 2026. 
 2. Jury, competition and Étoile d’Or
 The 2026 jury is chaired by Marion Cotillard, the French actress and Oscar winner. The announcement was made on 13 October 2026, as the Moroccan press reported. The sources consulted do not publish the full list of the other jury members, so we name no one else.
 The international competition brings together 14 films, first and second features, according to the 2026 rules. The top prize, the Étoile d’Or, is worth USD 50,000. Film submissions closed on 31 July 2026, and the official selection is due to be announced « early in November 2026 ». Until it is published, no title can be presented as selected.
 The opening film, the closing film and the tributes had not been announced as of 21 October 2026. If a guide presents them as settled, check its publication date: it may be describing the 2025 edition.
 The 2025 context, not to be confused with 2026
 The 22nd edition ran from 28 November to 6 December 2025, under the presidency of Bong Joon-ho. Its opening film was Dead Man’s Wire , by Gus Van Sant, and its closing film Palestine 36 , by Annemarie Jacir. Tributes were paid to Jodie Foster and Guillermo del Toro, and the selection included 82 films from 31 countries. This information describes the 2025 edition: it does not predict the 2026 programme.
 Sources: Moroccan Cinema Centre (CCM), news item no. 2239 ; Le Matin, 2025 selection (in French) . Checked on 21 October 2026. 
 3. The Ateliers de l’Atlas, the professional strand
Photo by wong zihoo 
on Unsplash Ateliers de l’Atlas 2026, ninth edition
 22 to 26 November 2026 
 30 projects selected 
 14 countries represented 
 Sponsor: Kleber Mendonça Filho The Ateliers de l’Atlas, in their ninth edition, run from 22 to 26 November 2026. Their sponsor is the Brazilian filmmaker Kleber Mendonça Filho. The press reports that 30 projects and films were selected from 410 applications, from 14 countries. Atlas Press, part of the same programme, runs from 23 to 27 November.
 Atlas Station, for producers, selected 8 producers from 30 applications. Five Moroccan short films in post-production were chosen from 24 applications. These workshops are aimed at film professionals.
 2026 sponsor: Kleber Mendonça Filho, Brazilian filmmaker. 
 Atlas Station: 8 producers selected from 30 applications. 
 Workshops: 30 projects selected from 410 applications, 14 countries. 
 Pixidia tip: these workshops do not give access to public screenings. If you are coming to see films, focus on the competition and on the screenings announced by the Foundation. Source: Le360, 19 October 2026 (in French) , which cites the Foundation’s press release. Checked on 21 October 2026. 
 4. Where to see the films: venues, open air and access
 The festival is not limited to one venue. Three spaces come up in the sources: the Palais des Congrès, for the opening ceremony and the competition according to an unofficial source; the Le Colisée cinema, for retrospectives, also according to an unofficial source; and Jemaa el-Fna square, for open-air screenings according to the press. The sources consulted give no confirmation of these venues from the Foundation.
Photo by Jake Hills 
on Unsplash Palais des Congrès and Le Colisée
 Hivernage and Guéliz 
 Competition and retrospectives 
 Talks and screenings According to an unofficial source, Marrakech Cityguide, the Palais des Congrès hosts the opening ceremony, the competition and presentations in the Salle des Ministres. It sits at the western end of the Avenue de France, in the Hivernage district. According to the same guide, public access there is limited, but the red carpet can be seen from the street.
 The Le Colisée cinema, on rue Prince Moulay Rachid in Guéliz, hosts retrospectives, according to the same unofficial source. Its role in the 2026 edition is therefore not confirmed by the Foundation: check before you travel.
 Palais des Congrès: opening ceremony and competition, according to an unofficial source. 
 Le Colisée: retrospectives, according to an unofficial source. 
 Indicative journeys: about 10 minutes by taxi from Guéliz, 15 minutes from the medina. 
 Pixidia tip: journey times depend on traffic and the time of day. Allow a margin before an opening screening, and check the exact address of the Palais des Congrès on the Foundation’s website. 
Photo by Polina Kocheva 
on Unsplash Jemaa el-Fna square: open-air screenings, according to the press
 Free according to the press 
 Arrive an hour early 
 Cool nights According to Marrakech Cityguide and Riotimes, a giant screen set up on the Café Argana side is due to show films every evening of the festival, without booking and free of charge. Both sources give the same advice: arrive about an hour early to have a chance of a seat.
 The official site could not be consulted for this section. Free entry and 2026 times are therefore not confirmed by the Foundation. According to the press, this format already existed during the 2022 and 2023 editions.
 Screen set up on the Café Argana side of the square. 
 Access without booking, according to the press. 
 2026 times to be confirmed with the Foundation. 
 Pixidia tip: bring a warm layer for evening screenings. On average over 1991-2020, November nights drop to around 7.6 °C. The venues at a glance
 Festival venues, type of screening and announced ticketing Venue Screenings Indicative access Announced ticketing 
 Palais des Congrès (Hivernage) Opening ceremony and competition, according to an unofficial source About 10 min by taxi from Guéliz, 15 min from the medina Limited public access; 2026 prices not published 
 Le Colisée cinema (Guéliz) Retrospectives, according to an unofficial source About 5 min on foot from Place du 16 Novembre Booking announced; prices not published 
 Jemaa el-Fna square Open air, every evening (according to the press) Centre of the medina, arrive an hour early Free and without booking according to the press, to be confirmed 
 Source: Marrakech Cityguide and Riotimes (24 September 2026) , checked on 21 October 2026. Unofficial sources: check them before your visit. 
 Cinema screenings: 2026 ticketing not yet published
 The sources disagree on cinema screenings. Marrakech Cityguide mentions free screenings on booking, opening two to three weeks before the festival, with capacity that fills quickly. Riotimes, in an article dated 24 September 2026, describes paid screenings, « from 40 dirhams » at past editions, and notes that 2026 prices had not been published.
 Without official information, the most reliable approach is this: the Foundation publishes the cinema ticketing details as the festival approaches. Check the official site before you travel. Do not build your budget on the 40 dirham figure, which comes from earlier editions.
 5. Getting to Marrakech and getting around during the festival
 Marrakech-Menara airport offers several ways into the city: a bus shuttle, small and large taxis, a private transfer with driver, car hire and parking, according to the airport’s guide. The airport page gives neither prices nor journey times.
 Transfer prices are not reliably published. Confirm the price before you get into the vehicle.
 Source: Marrakech-Menara airport for the options, checked on 21 October 2026. 
 The medina is not accessible by car. If you stay in a riad, ask your accommodation for the drop-off point and directions for the last stretch on foot. This matters most in the evening, when you head to Jemaa el-Fna square.
 To get between the medina, Guéliz and Hivernage during the festival, a taxi is the simplest option. Marrakech Cityguide gives about 10 minutes between Guéliz and the Palais des Congrès, and 15 minutes from the medina. These times vary with traffic, and a last-minute booking can take longer late in the day.
 If you want to add sightseeing before or after the screenings, see our best day trips from Marrakech . For journey times, the safest option is to check at the time of booking, in your usual transport app or with your accommodation.
 6. E-pass and accreditations: who can register and when
 The public e-pass is free and open to all. It gives access to the films and to conversations with personalities, and it is reserved for people aged 18 and over. Registration opens on 26 October 2026, for the public as well as for professionals. Once the registration is validated, the e-pass and the access code are sent by email. They then need to be used in the Marrakech Festival App.
 For the press, registration closes on 31 October 2026. The official page gives no deadline for the public or for professionals: register as soon as it opens, on 26 October 2026.
 2026 accreditations according to the official page Type Cost Opens Closes Conditions 
 Public (e-pass) Free 26 October 2026 Not stated Aged 18 and over 
 Cinema professionals Not stated 26 October 2026 Not stated Online registration 
 Press Not stated Not stated 31 October 2026 Online registration 
 Source: official accreditation page of the Marrakech International Film Festival , checked on 21 October 2026. 
 If an intermediary offers you a paid e-pass, go through the official page: that is where the free registration is described.
 7. Budget: what is confirmed and what is not
 Public access to the films is free thanks to the e-pass. The rest of the budget depends on items that have not all been published for 2026. The table below separates what has been verified from what still needs confirming.
 Budget items for a stay around the festival, as of 21 October 2026 Item Amount Status 
 Public e-pass €0 Confirmed by the official page 
 Cinema screenings (Palais des Congrès, Colisée) Not published for 2026 Past editions from 40 dirhams (Riotimes) 
 Screenings on Jemaa el-Fna square Free according to the press To be confirmed by the Foundation 
 Private souks tour with guide (Viator) €39.38 per adult, based on 2 adults Checked on 21 October 2026: open on the calendar on all 9 festival days, confirmed at booking for 20, 21, 23, 24, 26 and 28 November 
 Airport transfer Not published To be confirmed before departure 
 Source: festival accreditations , Riotimes (24 September 2026) , Viator availability and price checked on 21 October 2026. 
 The real budget therefore depends mostly on accommodation, meals and transport, for which no 2026 rate has been verified here. Two practical levers exist. First, Jemaa el-Fna square costs nothing according to the press, which keeps evenings inexpensive. Second, if the Foundation opens cinema ticketing, capacity fills quickly according to Marrakech Cityguide: it is best to book as soon as sales open.
 8. A possible four-day plan
 No screening schedule had been published as of 21 October 2026, so this plan does not set film times. It is there to organise your travel and the highlights of the stay.
 Day one: arrive and get your bearings
 To find the Palais des Congrès in Hivernage before the screening days, make the trip from your accommodation: allow about 10 minutes by taxi from Guéliz, according to Marrakech Cityguide, an indication that varies with traffic. Check that your e-pass registration was made from 26 October, and that the access code is saved in the app.
 Day two: the medina, then the square
 Book the souks tour for late morning, to discover the medina with a guide. In the evening, head to Jemaa el-Fna square. Arrive about an hour before the screenings are due to start, if the press has the organisation right, and dress warmly.
 Day three: the cinemas
 If cinema ticketing is open, book your screening as soon as possible: according to Marrakech Cityguide, capacity fills quickly. Allow travel time between Guéliz and Hivernage, which varies with traffic. A taxi remains the simplest way back late in the evening.
 Day four: departure
 Confirm the fare of your airport transfer before you leave. Ask your riad for the drop-off point nearest the medina, as vehicles do not enter it.
 9. Depending on your profile
 With family. The e-pass is reserved for people aged 18 and over, so younger people cannot register themselves. Focus the family programme on the medina, on Jemaa el-Fna square in the early evening, and on taxi trips.
 As a couple. Free screenings on Jemaa el-Fna square, according to the press, make for an evening with no ticket cost. For the private souks tour, the checked price of €39.38 per adult is based on two adults.
 On a small budget. The e-pass is free, the square screenings are free according to the press, and cinema screenings remain to be confirmed. The items to compare are accommodation and transport.
 For a first visit. Prioritise the medina during the day and one evening screening, and keep a time margin for journeys, which vary by hour. To choose outings outside the medina, see our selection of experiences in Marrakech beyond the medina .
 For cinema professionals. Professional registration is open from 26 October. The Ateliers de l’Atlas, from 22 to 26 November, are the event to follow, alongside the official selection expected in early November.
 10. Mistakes to avoid
 Mixing up the editions. The Bong Joon-ho jury, Dead Man’s Wire and Palestine 36 belong to the 2025 edition. They do not describe the 2026 festival.
 Confusing it with MARRAKECHsFF. That short film festival is separate and takes place in September.
 Taking the 40 dirham figure for a 2026 price. It comes from past editions, according to Riotimes.
 Relying on a third-party calendar for the dates. Some online listings give other dates: the official page and the 2026 rules do not confirm them.
 Looking for screening times in the press rather than with the Foundation. The programme and the ticketing will be published by the Foundation as the festival approaches.
 What other guides don’t tell you
 Several guides consulted leave out or misdate the following points. Each one points to an official source or to a precise consultation date.
 The public e-pass is free and opens on 26 October 2026. The accreditation page states it, whereas Riotimes refers to tickets going on sale « near the festival » without mentioning the e-pass ( official accreditations , consulted on 21 October 2026).
 Press registration closes on 31 October 2026. This date is missing from the guides read ( official accreditations , consulted on 21 October 2026).
 The Étoile d’Or is worth USD 50,000. The 2026 rules give the amount, which Riotimes and Mesloisirs do not mention ( 2026 rules , consulted on 21 October 2026).
 The 2026 jury is chaired by Marion Cotillard , announced on 13 October 2026. The Riotimes article of 24 September 2026 did not mention it yet ( Le360 (in French) , consulted on 21 October 2026).
 Film submissions closed on 31 July 2026, and the selection is expected in early November. Some online listings give 27 November to 5 December 2026: this date is contradicted by the rules and the official page ( 2026 rules , consulted on 21 October 2026).
 Practical information for your stay
 Before you leave, check the UK government’s travel advice for Morocco on GOV.UK, last updated on 19 August 2026, for entry rules. We do not state a passport validity figure here, because the rules change: the official page is the reference. GOV.UK, Morocco travel advice , checked on 21 October 2026.

 Frequently asked questions about the Marrakech Film Festival 2026
 When is the Marrakech Film Festival 2026? The festival runs from 20 to 28 November 2026, for its 23rd edition. These dates appear on the official accreditation page and are confirmed by the 2026 rules and the press. The Ateliers de l’Atlas, the professional strand, run from 22 to 26 November. No public screening date had been published as of 21 October 2026.
 Who chairs the jury of the Marrakech Film Festival 2026? The 2026 jury is chaired by Marion Cotillard, the French actress and Oscar winner. The announcement was made on 13 October 2026. The full list of the other members is not published in the sources consulted. Bong Joon-ho chaired the jury of the 2025 edition, which ran from 28 November to 6 December 2025.
 How do you attend the Marrakech Film Festival? The public gets access to the films and to conversations with personalities with a free e-pass, open to people aged 18 and over. Registration opens on 26 October 2026. Once validated, it generates an e-pass and an access code sent by email, to be used in the Marrakech Festival App. Open-air screenings on Jemaa el-Fna square are described as free by the press.
 What is the programme of the Marrakech Film Festival 2026? The detailed programme had not been published as of 21 October 2026. The official selection is due to be announced in early November, and the Foundation will publish the programme and ticketing as the festival approaches. A film list that does not cite the Foundation should be checked before you rely on it.
 How much does the Marrakech Film Festival cost? The public e-pass is free. For cinema screenings, no 2026 price had been published at the time of writing. Riotimes cites prices « from 40 dirhams » at past editions. Open-air screenings on Jemaa el-Fna square are described as free by the press, without official confirmation. Allow a margin for cinema tickets.
 Where are the festival screenings held? According to an unofficial source, the Palais des Congrès in Hivernage hosts the opening ceremony and the competition, and the Le Colisée cinema in Guéliz screens retrospectives. Jemaa el-Fna square hosts open-air screenings every evening, according to the press. None of these venues has yet been confirmed by the Foundation.
 How do you get from Marrakech airport to the festival? The airport offers a bus shuttle, taxis, a private transfer with driver, car hire and parking. Confirm the price before you leave. Inside the medina, vehicles do not enter: ask your riad for the drop-off point.
 What is the difference from MARRAKECHsFF? MARRAKECHsFF is a separate festival dedicated to short films, held in September. It is distinct from the Marrakech International Film Festival in November, which this guide covers. Do not confuse the two in your searches or your bookings.
 What is the weather like in November in Marrakech? On average over 1991-2020, November is around 21.7 °C by day and 7.6 °C at night, with 36.9 mm of rain spread over 5.3 days. These figures come from ERA5 reanalysis data calculated locally, not from a weather station. They give an order of magnitude, not a forecast.
 Sources
 Festival accreditations, Marrakech International Film Festival : e-pass, dates and registration calendar (consulted on 21 October 2026)
 2026 festival rules : film submissions, competition, Étoile d’Or (PDF, April 2026)
 Le360, 2026 jury : announcement of the presidency (13 October 2026, in French)
 Le360, Ateliers de l’Atlas 2026 : sponsor, selection, dates (19 October 2026, in French)
 Marrakech Cityguide : venues, open-air screenings, access (unofficial source)
 Riotimes : cinema ticketing and prices at past editions (24 September 2026)
 La Tribune de Marrakech : event listing, dates and link to the official site
 Marrakech-Menara airport : transport options, no prices
 GOV.UK, Morocco travel advice : entry rules (last updated 19 August 2026)
 Viator: price and availability of the private souks tour, retrieved via the partner API on 21 October 2026
 Moroccan Cinema Centre, news item no. 2239 : 2025 edition
 Open-Meteo, ERA5 archive : November climate over 1991-2020, local calculation
 Research and checks carried out on 21 October 2026.
